title: Projects whose budget and finish date moved, report by report
question: Which capital projects' cost forecasts and finish dates moved most across the reports their own departments published, and which rose report after report?
finding: 305 projects of $1 million or more appear in three or more dated reports. 77 now stand a quarter or more above their first figure and 114 are forecast to finish two years or more after the first date given; 0 rose in at least half of their reports and 27 rose in three or more. Leaving aside 13 continuing renewal programmes, the largest move is SEP Biosolids Digester Facilities Project (Public Utilities Commission), $1.68 billion to $2.84 billion over 14 reports from 2020-12 to 2026-06, finish moved +20 months. Programme totals for the projects present in both the first and the latest report: Water Enterprise CIP (6 projects, 2020-09 to 2026-06): $1.15 billion to $2.94 billion (+155%); Central Subway Project (Third Street Light Rail Phase 2) (9 projects, 2015-03 to 2022-09): $3.29 billion to $4.33 billion (+32%); Wastewater Enterprise CIP / SSIP (13 projects, 2020-09 to 2026-06): $1.68 billion to $2.04 billion (+21%); WSIP (Regional) / Appendix B project list (51 projects, 2024-09 to 2026-06): $3.33 billion to $3.33 billion (-0%). These are project budgets, which include design, management and land as well as construction; a rise can be added scope as well as higher cost, and the reports name the builder on few of them.
how: Every row of the capital reports on disk that gives a project, a report date and a cost was put in date order by project: the Public Utilities Commission's quarterly reports on its water, sewer and power programmes, the Central Subway progress reports and transit bond-oversight reports, the Public Works earthquake-safety bond reports, and Airport and Port capital reports. The cost is the forecast or final cost where the report prints one, otherwise the current approved budget. The first figure is the baseline budget or contract award value where a report prints it, otherwise the forecast in the first report on disk; the first finish date is the baseline or approved date in the first report, the latest is the forecast or actual date in the last. Projects need three dated reports and a first figure of $1 million; a figure more than twenty times or less than a fifth of the first is treated as a misreading and the project left out. "Rose" counts report-to-report steps in which the cost went up by more than 0.5%. Seasons printed as dates ("Fall 2028") are placed mid-season.
limits: Reports are not on disk for every quarter, and the first report on disk is usually not the project's first, so the starting figure can already include earlier growth. The Public Utilities Commission's "approved" finish date is the current approved schedule, not the original. Figures are copied from text layers and some scanned pages; units differ between reports and are converted as each report states them. A budget that rises because the Commission added work, or a date that moves because a project was deliberately resequenced, looks the same here as an overrun.
